paragraphs.text: Y562 is a named export recipe from the Yunnan Tea Import and Export Company, sold under its Jixing brand, a word meaning fortune. In the old coding the Y marks the company and the number stands for leaf grade and factory. Grade 5 to 6 points to fine, tender leaf, here from Menghai in southern Yunnan.

The leaf was made into [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) by [wet piling](shou:wet-piling), a method Yunnan’s state factories brought into production in 1973, which puts this lot in the style’s second decade. Rather than being pressed, it was kept loose in a 100 gram box, and it has sat in Hong Kong dry storage since around 1993.
At thirty-three years it falls among what the trade counts as [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged), where clean, dry keeping shapes the leaf as much as the years do.

brewing.text: The leaf is loose, so there is nothing to break off. Use boiling water, about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens. Ripe tea forgives a heavy hand, and gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
